:
Aggrieved by the award dated 04.06.2008 in O.P.No.525 of 2006 passed by the Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum V Additional District Judge at Karimnagar, the insurance company has preferred MACMA No.2759 of 2008 questioning the compensation and the claimants have filed Cross-Objections No.46222 of 2008 seeking enhancement of the compensation.
2. Having heard Mr. Srinivas Rao Vutla, learned counsel for the Insurance Company and Mr.
Venkateshwar Varanasi, learned counsel for the Claimants, perused the entire material on record.
3.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The claim petition is filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- on account of the death of the deceased in the motor vehicle accident.
The case of the claimant is that the deceased was aged about 42 years and was an agriculturist earning an amount of Rs.8,000/- per month.
The deceased and first respondent are known to each other and LK, J MACMA_2759_2008 and 2 Cross-Objection close friends.

On 26.06.2005 at 08.00 AM, on the instructions of the first respondent the deceased was proceeding on the motor cycle belonging to the first respondent, and on the way when he reached near Vamshi Book Center, Jammikunta, he met with an accident and received fractured injuries all over the body parts.
Basing on the same the claimants have claimed the compensation.
In support of their case claimants have got examined Pws.1 and 2 and got marked Exs.A1 to A5.
On behalf of the respondent/insurance company, Rw.1 was examined and Exs.B1 and B2 were marked.

4. The case of the Insurance Company is that as the deceased stepped into the shoes of the owner of the vehicle and as there is no other vehicle involved in the accident, as he himself is a tortfeasor, he cannot claim the compensation.

However the Court below held that the accident was out of the negligence of the driver of the other motor cycle, still the claim petition is maintainable since the claimants are seeking compensation under Section 163-A of MV Act, where the rash and negligent driving is not a criteria for the purpose of LK, J MACMA_2759_2008 and 3 Cross-Objection awarding compensation and granted an amount of Rs.1,73,000/-.

sentences.text: Learned Counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submitted that the Court below failed to observe that the claim of compensation for death of a person who himself is responsible for the accident is not maintainable even under Section 163-A of the Act.

Further it is submitted that as per the Insurance policy, the risk of the persons travelling on insured vehicle is not covered and the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation for the death of the deceased who was driving the Insured vehicle at the time of the accident.
He has relied on the Judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Ramkhiladi vs The United India Insurance1 and submits that the Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation.

entities.text: Ramkhiladi vs The United India Insurance1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. In this case, the deceased was driving the vehicle which belonged to the first respondent in the claim petition.
Even as per the claimants, because of the negligence on the part of the driver of the vehicle, the accident has taken place.
There is no 1 (AIR 2020 SC 527) LK, J MACMA_2759_2008 and 4 Cross-Objection other vehicle involved in the accident.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Court below has observed that under Section 163-A of the Act, rash and negligent need not be proved and the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation on this issue, the Hon'ble Apex Court in Ramkhiladi's case (stated supra) has observed as below:
"Now, so far as the submission made on behalf of the claimants that in a claim under Section 163A of the Act mere use of the vehicle is enough and despite the compensation claimed by the heirs of the owner of the motorcycle which was involved in the accident resulting in his death, the claim under Section 163A of the Act would be maintainable is concerned, in view of the decision of this Court in Rajni Devi (supra), the aforesaid cannot be accepted.

In Rajni Devi (supra), it has been specifically observed and held that the provisions of Section 163A of the Act cannot be said to have any application with regard to an accident wherein the owner of the motor vehicle himself is involved.

After considering the decisions of this Court in the cases of Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. V. Jhuma Saha (2007) 9 SCC 263; Dhanraj (supra); National Insurance Co. Ltd. V. Laxmi Narain Dhut (2007) 3 LK, J MACMA_2759_2008 and 5 Cross-Objection SCC 700 and Premkumari v. Prahlad Dev (2008) 3 SCC 193, it is ultimately concluded by this Court that the liability under Section 163A of the Act is on the owner of the vehicle as a person cannot be both, a claimant as also a recipient and, therefore, the heirs of the owner could not have maintained the claim in terms of Section 163A of the Act.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. V. Jhuma Saha (2007) 9 SCC 263
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. V. Laxmi Narain Dhut (2007) 3 LK
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further observed that, for the said purpose, only the terms of the contract of insurance could be taken recourse to.

In the recent decision of this Court in the case of Ashalata Bhowmik (supra), it is specifically held by this Court that the parties shall be governed by the terms and conditions of the contract of insurance.

Therefore, as per the contract of insurance, the insurance company shall be liable to pay the compensation to a third party and not to the owner, except to the extent of Rs.1 lakh as observed hereinabove".
7.

In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Ramkhiladi's case (stated supra), at best as the deceased was driving the vehicle at the time of the accident and stepped in to the shoes of the owner, the claimants are entitled for the accident coverage of Rs.1,00,000/- as per the policy.
